bib.title: Rethinking the Inception Architecture for Computer Vision

question: How can convolutional networks be scaled up so that added computation is used efficiently, via factorized convolutions and aggressive regularization?
hypothesis: Following four design principles (avoid early bottlenecks, higher-dimensional local representations, spatial aggregation over reduced embeddings, balanced width/depth) plus factorization and regularization yields higher accuracy at modest cost; the authors call the principles speculative.
contributions: Four general design principles for scaling conv nets
Factorizing 5x5 into two 3x3 and n x n into 1 x n + n x 1
Auxiliary classifiers reinterpreted as regularizers (batch-normalized side head)
Inception-v2/v3 with 21.2% top-1 / 5.6% top-5 single-crop on ILSVRC 2012

method.summary: Redesigns the GoogLeNet/Inception architecture with factorized convolutions, efficient grid reduction, a batch-normalized auxiliary classifier and label smoothing (epsilon 0.1, uniform prior), trained with RMSProp on ImageNet; ablations are cumulative in Table 3.

datasets.name: ILSVRC 2012 classification
datasets.size: 1000 classes; train size not stated; validation evaluated on 48238 non-blacklisted examples (of 50000)
datasets.split: validation set for all reported numbers; test-set check promised for a later version

models.name: Inception-v2 / Inception-v3 (last row of Table 3)
models.architecture: convolutional, Inception modules with factorized convs; 299x299x3 input

other.cost: 5 billion multiply-adds per inference; 4.8 Bn Ops in Table 3
other.structure: 3 Inception at 35x35 (288 filters), 5 at 17x17 (768), 2 at 8x8 (1280 to 2048 concat); n=7 for the 17x17 grid; detailed filter sizes only in supplementary model.txt

training.objective: cross entropy with label-smoothing regularization: q'(k)=(1-eps)delta_{k,y}+eps/K, eps=0.1, K=1000
training.optimizer: RMSProp decay 0.9, epsilon 1.0 for best models; earlier experiments used momentum with decay 0.9
training.lr_schedule: decayed every two epochs with exponential rate 0.94
training.dropout: dropout layer in the auxiliary head is mentioned as helping, rate not stated
training.regularisation: label smoothing eps 0.1; batch-normalized auxiliary classifier; gradient clipping threshold 2.0; evaluation uses running average of parameters
training.hardware: 50 replicas, each on one NVidia Kepler GPU, TensorFlow distributed

inference.samples: single crop (Table 3); 12 or 144 crops (Table 4); ensemble of 4 models with 144 crops (Table 5)

metrics.name: Top-1 error
metrics.definition: fraction of validation images where the top prediction is wrong

metrics.name: Top-5 error
metrics.definition: fraction where true label not in top 5

eval.protocol: Single run, no seeds or significance tests; evaluated on 48238 non-blacklisted validation examples; all 50000 gives roughly 0.1% worse top-5 and 0.2% worse top-1.

availability.code: model.txt in submission tar-file (supplementary), not a public link
